maxErrorsPerGroup.description:
Maximum number of stored error objects per (model, property, errorType)
group. Quality errors are still counted exactly beyond this limit and are
reachable via `dcupl.quality.errors.summary()` or the
`$DcuplErrorTrackingSummary` model; only the retained error objects (and
the `$DcuplErrorTrackingErrors` model) are bounded. Retained records of a
capped group carry `truncated: true` and `groupTotal`. Default: 1000.

Note: for error groups whose true count exceeds `maxErrorsPerGroup`,
partial-update cleanup may cause the totals to slightly
over-report, since over-cap occurrences are counted but never stored as
error objects and therefore cannot be decremented on removal.

containerBatchSize.description:
Controls async/sync processing mode for containers:
- undefined (default): Async mode - yield after every container (backward compatible)
- 0: Synchronous mode - never yield (best performance, may block UI)
- N > 0: Batched mode - yield every N containers (balanced performance)

Note: Synchronous/batched modes are opt-in optimizations. Use only if your
application can handle synchronous processing without UI blocking.
containerBatchSize.title: containerBatchSize

autoUpdateLists.description:
Controls whether lists automatically update when affected by data changes.
When enabled, lists automatically call update() when their data changes.
When disabled, manual list.update() calls are required.

Can be overridden at list-level or per-update.

autoGenerateProperties.description:
Configures how property auto-generation inspects input data.

- `true` / `false`: enable/disable auto-generation. When enabled with `true`,
  only the first row of input data is inspected (fast, default behavior).
- Object form lets you scan more rows:
  - `deep: true` walks every row and reconciles types across them.
  - `sampleSize: N` walks at most N rows (implies deep). Useful for large datasets
    where row 1 alone may not represent the schema.

When more than one row is scanned, empty values (`null`, `undefined`, `''`)
are ignored during inference so a single blank cell does not poison a column's type.
autoGenerateProperties.title: autoGenerateProperties

anyOf.description: Equality query - matches exact values.

Membership query - matches if the attribute's value equals **any** value of
the list, using the same equality as `eq`: a string (or `{ key }`) matches a
reference by its key and a date by its ISO string. It answers like an `or`
group of one `eq` condition per listed value.

- On an `Array<…>` property or a dotted path through a multi-valued
  reference, `arrayValueHandling: 'some'` (default) matches if at least one
  value is listed; `'every'` if every value is listed (and there is at least one).
- `options.invert` is NOT IN; like `eq`, a missing value then matches.
- `options.transform` applies to the attribute value and to every listed value.
- `null` in the list matches `null`, like `eq` with `null`.
- An empty list matches nothing (and everything under `invert`).
- `value` must be an array; anything else throws. (`eq` with an array value
  compares the whole array instead.)

Find query - regex / exact / object match.

Matching depends on the shape of `value`:
- **Bare string** (e.g. `'search'`) — exact-equality against the *whole* field
  value, NOT a substring. `find` with `'Ball'` does not match `'Soccer Ball'`.
- **Slash-delimited regex** (e.g. `'/search/'`, `'/^foo/'`) — the text between the
  slashes is a JS regex; use this for substring and pattern matching. Flags go in
  `options.regexFlags` (`'/^foo/'` + `regexFlags: 'i'`), not after the closing
  slash: `'/^foo/i'` is a bare string and matches exactly.
- **Object** (e.g. `{ key: 'value' }`) — property matching against the field.

Numeric/date comparison queries.
Supports greater than, less than, and inclusive variants.
Type check query - validates data type.
Truthiness check query - evaluates boolean truthiness.
Size check query - matches array length or string length.

Options for executing queries across the global dcupl instance.
Combines model specification, query conditions, and data retrieval options.

Query group - combines multiple conditions with AND/OR logic.
Groups can be nested to create complex filter expressions.

groupType.description:
Combination logic for conditions in this group.

Defaults to `'and'` at evaluation time: a group that reaches the query engine without a
groupType (the root query, or a nested group passed inside a full query via
`apply({ groupKey: 'root', ... })`, `init` or `execute`, or stored by `setGroup`
replacing an existing group) is evaluated exactly like `groupType: 'and'`.

Note that groups *created* by the query builder (`addGroup` / `setGroup` / `apply(group)`
for a group not yet present) are stored as `'or'` when no groupType is given, and
`addGroup` extending an existing keyed group keeps that group's current groupType. Set
the groupType explicitly to avoid depending on either default.
groupType.title: groupType

groupKey.description:
Optional identifier for this group.
Useful for tracking or removing specific query groups. Adding a group with an
existing groupKey extends that group; a group without groupKey is always added
as a new group.
groupKey.title: groupKey

transform.description:
Transform value before comparison.
Applied in order: ['lowercase', 'trim'] applies lowercase first, then trim.
transform.title: transform

invert.description:
Invert the query result (NOT operation). Applies to every built-in operator.
A missing (`undefined`/`null`) value matches neither way, except for `eq`,
`in`, `typeof` and `isTruthy`, which compare against it. A list of values (an
`Array<…>` property or a dotted path through a multi-valued reference) is
checked per value instead: an empty list, or a `null` in it, simply does not
match, so `invert` does match it (`memberships.user.daysInactive gte 60`
inverted includes items with no memberships).
invert.title: invert

arrayValueHandling.description:
When querying array values, determines match behavior. Array values are
`Array<…>` properties and dotted paths through a multi-valued reference
(`memberships.role` compares the `role` of every membership).
- `some`: Match if at least one array element matches (default)
- `every`: Match only if all array elements match — and there is at least
  one: an empty array (or a reference with no items) never matches

On a reference path, leaves that are `undefined` are skipped.
arrayValueHandling.title: arrayValueHandling

value.description:
Value to match against.
Note: For indexed search optimization, use string or { key: string } values.
value.title: value

groupType.description:
Combination logic for conditions in this group.

Defaults to `'and'` at evaluation time: a group that reaches the query engine without a
groupType (the root query, or a nested group passed inside a full query via
`apply({ groupKey: 'root', ... })`, `init` or `execute`, or stored by `setGroup`
replacing an existing group) is evaluated exactly like `groupType: 'and'`.

Note that groups *created* by the query builder (`addGroup` / `setGroup` / `apply(group)`
for a group not yet present) are stored as `'or'` when no groupType is given, and
`addGroup` extending an existing keyed group keeps that group's current groupType. Set
the groupType explicitly to avoid depending on either default.
groupType.title: groupType

groupKey.description:
Optional identifier for this group.
Useful for tracking or removing specific query groups. Adding a group with an
existing groupKey extends that group; a group without groupKey is always added
as a new group.

DcuplQuery.description:
Query condition - represents a single filter criterion.
Use this to filter items based on attribute values.
DcuplQuery.title: DcuplQuery

anyOf.description: Equality query - matches exact values.

Membership query - matches if the attribute's value equals **any** value of
the list, using the same equality as `eq`: a string (or `{ key }`) matches a
reference by its key and a date by its ISO string. It answers like an `or`
group of one `eq` condition per listed value.

- On an `Array<…>` property or a dotted path through a multi-valued
  reference, `arrayValueHandling: 'some'` (default) matches if at least one
  value is listed; `'every'` if every value is listed (and there is at least one).
- `options.invert` is NOT IN; like `eq`, a missing value then matches.
- `options.transform` applies to the attribute value and to every listed value.
- `null` in the list matches `null`, like `eq` with `null`.
- An empty list matches nothing (and everything under `invert`).
- `value` must be an array; anything else throws. (`eq` with an array value
  compares the whole array instead.)

Find query - regex / exact / object match.

Matching depends on the shape of `value`:
- **Bare string** (e.g. `'search'`) — exact-equality against the *whole* field
  value, NOT a substring. `find` with `'Ball'` does not match `'Soccer Ball'`.
- **Slash-delimited regex** (e.g. `'/search/'`, `'/^foo/'`) — the text between the
  slashes is a JS regex; use this for substring and pattern matching. Flags go in
  `options.regexFlags` (`'/^foo/'` + `regexFlags: 'i'`), not after the closing
  slash: `'/^foo/i'` is a bare string and matches exactly.
- **Object** (e.g. `{ key: 'value' }`) — property matching against the field.

Numeric/date comparison queries.
Supports greater than, less than, and inclusive variants.
Type check query - validates data type.
Truthiness check query - evaluates boolean truthiness.
Size check query - matches array length or string length.

autoGenerateProperties.description:
Configures how property auto-generation inspects input data.

- `true` / `false`: enable/disable auto-generation. When enabled with `true`,
  only the first row of input data is inspected (fast, default behavior).
- Object form lets you scan more rows:
  - `deep: true` walks every row and reconciles types across them.
  - `sampleSize: N` walks at most N rows (implies deep). Useful for large datasets
    where row 1 alone may not represent the schema.

When more than one row is scanned, empty values (`null`, `undefined`, `''`)
are ignored during inference so a single blank cell does not poison a column's type.
